client: HitoAI Limited, an Irish AI and EdTech company
description: The public platform for HitoAI, an Irish AI company with a portfolio of products across education, health, marketing and energy. One site presents every product on a page of its own, catalogues the AI APIs the company offers, and runs applications for its EEP programme from form to inbox.
role: Full-stack engineer: built the site, the application backend and the admin screens
contributions: Built the whole front end in React and TypeScript: landing, about with the board and team, services, contact, and sign-in and register
Built a page for each product in the portfolio: EEP, SusNet, AI4Physio, AIMarcom, 223D, Knomed, Secuall and Selwell
Built the API catalogue and documentation pages for the company's AI services (prediction, NLP, vision, conversational)
Built the EEP application flow: a form with CV upload, an Express API that emails the application and CV to the team, and a confirmation email to the applicant
Wrote the terms and conditions flow for applicants, including the NDA
Built admin screens for managing clients, staff and projects
Added an assistant chat on every page
results: One site for a portfolio of 8 AI products
Applications go from the form to the team's inbox with the CV attached, and the applicant gets a confirmation
First version up in four days, then extended over three months

body.heading: The brief
paragraphs: HitoAI is an Irish company run by academics in AI, with a growing set of products: a learning and mentorship programme (EEP), energy forecasting (SusNet), AI-assisted physiotherapy (AI4Physio), marketing (AIMarcom), 3D model generation (223D), and more.

The site had to explain the company and every product clearly to partners, funders and future students in one place, and take applications for the EEP programme without a spreadsheet and a shared inbox.

body.heading: One site, many products
paragraphs: Each product gets its own page with the same shape: what it is, who it is for, the features that matter, and how to get involved. That made the portfolio easy to scan and made adding the next product a matter of content, not design.

Around them sit the company pages: the board and team, the services HitoAI offers, and a catalogue of the AI APIs it can build or provide (prediction and anomaly detection, natural-language processing, computer vision, conversational AI), with a documentation section behind it.

body.heading: Applications that arrive complete
paragraphs: The EEP programme takes applicants, so the site needed more than a contact form. Applicants fill in their details, agree to the terms and the NDA, and upload a CV. A small Express API receives it, emails the application to the team with the CV attached, and sends the applicant a confirmation, both from templated emails.
Nobody has to chase a missing CV or reply to say an application arrived: it lands in one inbox complete, and the applicant knows it did.

body.heading: Built with
paragraphs: React and TypeScript on Vite, styled with Tailwind and shadcn/ui, deployed on Vercel. The application API is Node.js and Express with Multer for uploads, Nodemailer with EJS templates for the emails, and Helmet and CORS in front; MongoDB is set up for storing what comes in.
